habitat: Pairs in mixed bushveld and any woodland, and particularly in suburbia. The male sings for long periods from a prominent perch.
summary: A common resident. The colour key says the head, breast and mantle are glossy blue, the belly white, and the bill a curved black one. The matching description says the male has an iridescent blue-green head, mantle, throat and breast, plus white underparts. The female is like a female Dusky Sunbird, with underparts less clearly white. An immature male may have pale yellow underparts and a blue throat-patch. The song is chu-ee, chu-ee, chuee-trrrrrr, or ta-la, ta-la, ta-la, trrrr, and the page says the scientific name comes from that phrase. That description is printed on the Malachite page. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

head.pattern: Iridescent blue-green head, throat and breast. The colour key says glossy blue.

upperparts.pattern: Glossy blue mantle, described as iridescent blue-green. Blue-green is not a single token.

underparts.pattern: White underparts. The breast is part of the glossy blue-green area.

calls.description: A loud song, chu-ee, chu-ee, chuee-trrrrrr, or ta-la, ta-la, ta-la, trrrr, repeated often. The Malachite page says the scientific name comes from that phrase. Grade A call from Hoedspruit. The filename is XC549784-White-bellied Sunbird RV 200423-070600.mp3.

research.note: The colour key and the 11 cm size are on the White-bellied page. The sexed plumage and the song are printed on the Malachite page, and that page ties the song to the scientific name, which is why this needs review. Dusky Sunbird and Plain-backed Sunbird are comparisons and are not in this list. Population figures and the Kemp code RB were left unchanged.
